assets.sizeEvidence: ESTABLISHED by a stated source: Sidoroff, EXARC Journal, 'Large individual pieces of camel dung measured 7 cm x 5 cm, the weight of 6 pieces was 0.175 kg' and 'Smaller pieces measured 3cm x 2 cm, the weight of 6 pieces was 0.020 kg'. Bedouin-sourced dung, southern Jordan. Derived, not stated: about 29 g and 3.3 g per piece, and about 0.32 and 0.53 g/cm3 if treated as ellipsoids, so very light. Pixel cross-check (derived, read by eye): the bucket photo exarc_i7_bucket.jpg, with the stated bucket diameter of 24 cm spanning about 690 px at the rim (about 29 px/cm), gives rounded pieces of about 3.0 to 3.8 cm and lumps of about 4.7 to 5.6 cm. Pieces sit below the rim plane, so these read slightly low. One Jordanian lot, not a species range; no Kutch or Rajasthan measurement found. The AZM, Qatar and Kutch photos have no calibrated scale.
assets.shape: Separate pellets, egg, bean or near-round, with no fixed form. Qatar photo: elongated eggs, length to width about 1.2 to 1.7 by eye, wide size spread (largest about 2.3 times the smallest in frame). Kutch photo: rounder, but the view is oblique. The AZM profile says: 'Camels produce round pellets, usually in large numbers. The pellets have bits of plant material in them.' Colour varies strongly by photo: glossy black (AZM), dark moist (Bactrian), grey wrinkled (Qatar), pale silt-coated (Kutch), pale buff (Jordan). The photos do not establish why, so age or wetness as the cause is a hypothesis.
assets.surface: Dry state: fine crazed wrinkles across a matt skin, longitudinal creases, torn seams with tan plant fibre showing, loose fibre strands, adhering sand or silt. Dark state: smooth, specular, with grit stuck on.

assets.sizeEvidence: Source statement: Hong Kong CMM Standards row already in substance-looks: roots 3.5-24 cm long, 1-10 mm diameter. Derived from scale bars in photos, measured by me, about +/-10%, and not true 3D: 53847-2 at 88 px/cm: pieces about 4.1, 5.6 and 4.6 cm long. A distance-transform on the mask gives diameter p10 5.9, p50 8.5, p90 14.3, max 16.9 mm. 53829-2 at 93 px/cm: diameter p10 1.5, p50 3.7, p90 6.1, max 11.1 mm; crown about 2.5 x 3.2 cm. 53861-2 (bar read off a contact sheet, about 93 px/cm, less exact): p10 2.2, p50 3.6, p90 4.9 mm. 53319-2 (about 97 px/cm, less exact): p10 2.5, p50 7.0, p90 9.4, max 14.5 mm. Ridge figures in lumpy areas also count crowns. 53297-1 at 71 px/cm: bundle about 7.4 x 4.2 cm, sticks about 2-3 mm by eye against the bar. Jar Y1970.90.33: museum states 170 x 75 mm overall, giving about 0.15 mm/px, so the sinuous root is about 4-6 mm, but curved glass may magnify. 92054-2 has no bar: not established. Commercial lengths in a dye workshop: not established.
assets.shape: Three forms were seen, and none is a smooth tube. (1) Whole dried roots (53829, 53319, 53861, jar, CMRO): knobbly crown heads with several thin kinked, wandering roots coming off; thickness changes along the length; some roots are nearly straight and some bend sharply. (2) Cut lengths (53847, 92054, trade photos, 53297): straight or gently curved cylinders with square or broken ends. (3) Tied bundles of cut sticks (53297, 100932). Size evidence is in sizeEvidence.
assets.surface: Matte and dry, with no gloss in any photo. Fine lengthwise grain and wrinkles run along the root. The outer bark is thin and flakes off in irregular patches, leaving a darker, rougher layer beneath (53847-2 centre piece). Cut or split places show orange to orange-red. Dark streaks occur along the bark (53829, 53861). Colour varies strongly by lot: tan-brown (53847, 53829), dark red-brown (53297), clean orange-brown (92054), grey-brown (100932). The current render's salmon colour matches no photo as an overall surface; orange appears only on cut and split faces, and on the clean 92054 sticks.
assets.limits: Kew images are 1600 px wide. At 88 px/cm the crop per piece is only about 400-500 px, so they cannot yield a 2K tile, and are detail sources rather than full PBR sets. Colour may have changed with age in museum lots, whose dates are mostly not given. Kew's own specimen pages were behind a browser challenge, so identity rests on GBIF's copy of the record and labels in photos. No photo shows madder in a working Ajrakh, Sanganeri or Machilipatnam workshop heap. No 3D model or PBR of madder root was found with a free no-login download. Poly Haven root_cluster_02 (seen) is tree roots in soil. dry_branches_medium_01 (seen) is tree branches about 1 m across. Neither is fit or downloaded; only previews are in downloads/ph. ambientCG has 16 bark materials and Poly Haven 24 bark textures (listed by API, not opened). Any would be proxy-only, and were not chosen. Build cannot reach: true microfibre at very close range, or real flake layering beyond the shell patches.

assets.shape: Sunk vat: a circular mouth, flush or with a thick raised collar about a hand's breadth wide, set in a slab; often covered by loose timber boards when idle; pole and rod lying in or by it. Mouth width looks arm's reach to a crouching adult in kc-6-1. Wash tanks: rectangular cement boxes, thick walled with flat copings, connected in a stepped row, stone kerbs, ledges inside.
assets.surface: Three states seen. New smooth pale cement with flaking skim (sanganeri-05: mid #9ea1a5). Dye-stained rust-brown with blotches (sanganeri-10: mid #773819, dry rim mid #90603c). Indigo-stained blue-grey slab (kc-6-1: mid #5b6369). Vat surface is not clean liquid: scum and bubbles, sampled mid #493f4e in jt-vat and #323c4a in kc-6-1. Bath water reads nearly black with sharp sky reflection.
assets.limits: Depth cannot be shown to the viewer; the interior goes black in the photos too. Real bubbles, foam motion, and cloth motion in water would be approximated. Sanganeri-05 and -10 are from a modern site. Machilipatnam tank photos were found only at 448 px, and text sources there describe washing in flowing water or a canal, so a tank may not be right for that route: check the stage text.

assets.sizeEvidence: Not measured. Text for pad layers, conflicting by workshop: "Colors used for printing are kept in a wooded tray called as saaj", "Once the color is poured into the tray wire mesh is placed inside. This mesh is covered with a piece of felt.", "Felt soaks the color and finally a fine cotton/malmal cloth is placed on the felt" (Meenal Design blog on Sanganer). assets.shape: Two table types were seen. A: waist-height timber frame with padded top and sewn skirt (Bagru, Machilipatnam). B: very low board (Ajrakh patiya) with the printer seated in a pit or on the ground. The tray is shallow and rectangular, dark wood or metal with a low rim, resting on a small stool or stand beside the table, or on a brick. The block rests on the side table.
assets.surface: Pad: looped towel-like cloth in kc-73, flat fine-weave cloth surface in sanganeri-08, or bare paste in gac-patiya. Colour is saturated where wet (kc-73 mid #999018, lit #cdc434) with a darker margin at the rim. Red paste in gac-patiya: mid #33120b. Table top dark sacking: mid #27292c. Skirt: multicolour stain on pale cloth, mid #d6d1cd. Table leg wood: mid #7c5d4a.
assets.limits: The sieve in the wire-mesh sense was not seen in any photograph; only described in text. Pad layer recipes differ by workshop and no single one is standard. The loaded look depends on a moving wet surface which a static mesh only suggests. The Kindcraft images are 1000 px, and GAC images 1200 px; they are weak as textures at close range.
